## General

## 1.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 1.1] This practice direction applies to Circuit Commercial claims.

## 1.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 1.2] Circuit Commercial Courts are established in –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 1.2] (1) the following district registries of the High Court – Birmingham, Bristol, Cardiff, Leeds, Liverpool, Manchester and Newcastle upon Tyne; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 1.2] (2) the Commercial Court of the King’s Bench Division at the Royal Courts of Justice (called ‘The London Circuit Commercial Court’).

## 1.3

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 1.3] All Circuit Commercial claims will be heard or determined by a Circuit Commercial  judge, except that –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 1.3] (1) an application may be heard and determined by any other judge who, if the claim were not a Circuit Commercial claim, would have jurisdiction to determine it, if –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 1.3] (a) the application is urgent and no Circuit Commercial judge is available to hear it; or

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 1.3] (b) a Circuit Commercial  judge directs it to be heard by another judge; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 1.3] (2) unless the court otherwise orders, all proceedings for the enforcement of a Circuit Commercial Court judgment or order for the payment of money will be dealt with by a district judge.

## 1.4

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 1.4] Provisions in other practice directions which refer to a master or district judge are to be read, in relation to Circuit Commercial claims, as if they referred to a Circuit Commercial  judge.

## Starting proceedings in a Circuit Commercial Court

## 2.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 2.1] A claim should only be started in a Circuit Commercial Court if it will benefit from the expertise of a Circuit Commercial  judge.

## 2.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 2.2] The claim form must be marked in the top right hand corner ‘Business and Property Courts in [………] In the High Court of Justice’ and either, Circuit Commercial Court (KBD)’, or ‘Business and Property Courts of England and Wales, London Circuit Commercial Court (KBD)’ as appropriate.

## 2.3

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 2.3] Omitted

## 2.4

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 2.4] Omitted

## Applications before proceedings are issued

## 3.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 3.1] A party who intends to bring a claim in a Circuit Commercial Court must make any application before the claim form is issued to a judge of that court.

## 3.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 3.2] The written evidence in support of such an application should show why the claim is suitable to proceed as a Circuit Commercial claim.

## Transfer of proceedings to or from a Circuit Commercial Court

## 4.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 4.1] If a claim which has not been issued in a Circuit Commercial Court is suitable to continue as a Circuit Commercial claim –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 4.1] (1) any party wishing the claim to be transferred to a Circuit Commercial Court may make an application for transfer to the court to which transfer is sought;

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 4.1] (2) if all parties consent to the transfer, the application may be made by letter to the Circuit Commercial listing officer of the court to which transfer is sought, stating why the case is suitable to be transferred to that court and enclosing the written consents of the parties, the claim form and statements of case.

## 4.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 4.2] If an application for transfer is made to a court which does not have power to make the order, that court may –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 4.2] (1) adjourn the application to be heard by a Circuit Commercial  judge; or

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 4.2] (2) dismiss the application.

## 4.3

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 4.3] A Circuit Commercial  judge may make an order under rule 59.3 of his own initiative.

## Default judgment and admissions

## 5.

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 5.] The practice directions supplementing Parts 12 and 14 apply with the following modifications –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 5.] (1) paragraph 4.1(1) of Practice Direction 12 is to be read as referring to the service of the claim form; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 5.] (2) the references to ‘particulars of claim’ in paragraphs 2.1, 3.1 and 3.2 of Practice Direction 14 are to be read as referring to the claim form.

## Variation of time limits by agreement

## 6.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 6.1] If the parties, in accordance with rule 2.11, agree in writing to vary a time limit, the claimant must notify the court in writing, giving brief written reasons for the agreed variation.

## 6.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 6.2] The court may make an order overriding an agreement by the parties varying a time limit.

## Case management

## 7.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.1] The following parts only of Practice Direction 29 apply –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.1] (1) paragraph 5 (case management conferences), excluding paragraph 5.9 and modified so far as is made necessary by other specific provisions of this practice direction; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.1] (2) paragraph 7 (failure to comply with case management directions).

## 7.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.2] If proceedings are started in a Circuit Commercial Court, the claimant must apply for a case management conference –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.2] (1) for a Part 7 claim, within 14 days of the date when all defendants who intend to file and serve a defence have done so; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.2] (2) for a Part 8 claim, within 14 days of the date when all defendants who intend to serve evidence have done so.

## 7.3

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.3] If proceedings are transferred to a Circuit Commercial Court, the claimant must apply for a case management conference within 14 days of receiving an acknowledgment of the transfer from the receiving court, unless the judge held, or gave directions for, a case management conference when he made the order transferring the proceedings.

## 7.4

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.4] Any party may, at a time earlier than that provided in paragraphs 7.2 or 7.3, apply in writing to the court to fix a case management conference.

## 7.5

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.5] If the claimant does not make an application in accordance with paragraphs 7.2 or 7.3, any other party may apply for a case management conference.

## 7.6

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.6] The court may fix a case management conference at any time on its own initiative. If it does so, the court will give at least 7 days notice to the parties, unless there are compelling reasons for a shorter period of notice.

## 7.7

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.7] Not less than 7 days before a case management conference –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.7] (1) each party shall file and serve –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.7] (a) a case management information sheet substantially in the form set out at Appendix A to this practice direction; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.7] (b) an application notice for any order which that party intends to seek at the case management conference, other than directions referred to in the case management information sheet; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.7] (2) the claimant (or other party applying for the conference) shall in addition file and serve –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.7] (a) a case management file containing –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.7] —  the claim form;

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.7] —   the statements of case (excluding schedules of more than 15 pages);

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.7] —   any orders already made;

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.7] —   the case management information sheets; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.7] —   a short list of the principal issues to be prepared by the claimant; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.7] (b) a draft order substantially in the form set out at Appendix B to this practice direction, setting out the directions which that party thinks appropriate.

## 7.8

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.8] In appropriate cases –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.8] (1) the parties may, not less than 7 days before the date fixed for the case management conference, submit agreed directions for the approval of the judge;

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.8] (2) the judge will then either –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.8] (a) make the directions proposed; or

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.8] (b) make them with alterations; or

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.8] (c) require the case management conference to proceed; but

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.8] (3) the parties must assume that the conference will proceed until informed to the contrary.

## 7.9

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.9] If the parties submit agreed directions and the judge makes them with alterations, any party objecting to the alterations may, within 7 days of receiving the order containing the directions, apply to the court for the directions to be varied.

## 7.10

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.10] The directions given at the case management conference –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.10] (1) will normally cover all steps in the case through to trial, including the fixing of a trial date or window, or directions for the taking of steps to fix the trial date or window; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.10] (2) may include the fixing of a progress monitoring date or dates, and make provision for the court to be informed as to the progress of the case at the date or dates fixed.

## 7.11

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.11] If the court fixes a progress monitoring date, it may after that date fix a further case management conference or a pre-trial review on its own initiative if –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.11] (1) no or insufficient information is provided by the parties; or

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 7.11] (2) it is appropriate in view of the information provided.

## Pre-trial review and questionnaire

## 8.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 8.1] The court may order a pre-trial review at any time.

## 8.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 8.2] Each party must file and serve a completed pre-trial check list substantially in the form set out in Appendix C to this practice direction –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 8.2] (1) if a pre-trial review has been ordered, not less than 7 days before the date of the review; or

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 8.2] (2) if no pre-trial review has been ordered, not less than 6 weeks before the trial date.

## 8.3

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 8.3] When pre-trial check lists are filed under paragraph 8.2(2) –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 8.3] (1) the judge will consider them and decide whether to order a pre-trial review; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 8.3] (2) if he does not order a pre-trial review, he may on his own initiative give directions for the further preparation of the case or as to the conduct of the trial.

## 8.4

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 8.4] At a pre-trial review –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 8.4] (1) the parties should if possible be represented by the advocates who will be appearing at the trial;

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 8.4] (2) any representatives appearing must be fully informed and authorised for the purposes of the review; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 8.4] (3) the court will give such directions for the conduct of the trial as it sees fit.

## Evidence for applications

## 9.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 9.1] The general requirement is that, unless the court orders otherwise –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 9.1] (1) evidence in support of an application must be filed and served with the application: see rule 23.7(3);

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 9.1] (2) evidence in answer must be filed and served within 14 days after the application is served;

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 9.1] (3) evidence in reply must be filed and served within 7 days of the service of the evidence in answer.

## 9.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 9.2] In any case in which the application is likely to require an oral hearing of more than half a day the periods set out in paragraphs 9.1(2) and (3) will be 28 days and 14 days respectively.

## 9.3

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 9.3] If the date fixed for the hearing of the application means that the times in paragraphs 9.1(2) and (3) cannot both be achieved, the evidence must be filed and served –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 9.3] (1) as soon as possible; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 9.3] (2) in sufficient time to ensure that the application may fairly proceed on the date fixed.

## 9.4

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 9.4] The parties may, in accordance with rule 2.11, agree different periods from those provided above, provided that the agreement does not affect the ability to proceed on the date fixed for the hearing of the application.

## Files for applications

## 10.

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 10.] Before the hearing of any application, the applicant must –

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 10.] (1) provide to the court and each other party an appropriate indexed file for the application with consecutively numbered pages; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 10.] (2) attach to the file an estimate of the reading time required by the judge.

## Judgments and orders

## 11.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 11.1] After any hearing the claimant must draw up a draft order, unless the decision was made on the application of another party in which case that party must do so.

## 11.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 11.2] A draft order must be submitted by the party responsible for drawing it up within 3 clear days of the decision, with sufficient copies for each party and for one to be retained by the court.

## 11.3

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 11.3] The sealed orders will be returned to the party submitting them, who will be responsible for serving the order on the other parties.

## 11.4

[This practice direction supplements Part 59 > 11.4] Orders must be dated with the date of the decision, except for consent orders submitted for approval, which must be left undated.
